Delete KVM's printk about KVM_SET_TSS_ADDR not being called.  When the
printk was added by commit 776e58ea3d37 (""KVM: unbreak userspace that does
not sets tss address"")
column2: KVM also stuffed a ""hopefully safe"" value

column1: the message wasn't purely informational.  For reasons unknown
to try and help people running outdated qemu-kvm versions
left behind when KVM's stuffing was removed by commit 4918c6ca6838
(""KVM: VMX: Require KVM_SET_TSS_ADDR being called prior to running a VCPU"").
Today
column3: as it has been over a decade

column1: since KVM supported userspace running a Real Mode guest
unrestricted guest support
I.e. KVM's ABI has required KVM_SET_TSS_ADDR for 10+ years.
To make matters worse
column2: the message is prone to false positives as it

column1: triggers when simply *creating* a vCPU due to RESET putting vCPUs into
Real Mode
column2: even when the user has no intention of ever *running* the vCPU

column1: in a Real Mode.  E.g. KVM selftests stuff 64-bit mode and never touch Real
Mode
column2: but trigger the message even though they run just fine without

column1: doing KVM_SET_TSS_ADDR.  Creating ""dummy"" vCPUs
can also trigger the message.  In both scenarios
users and falsely implies that they've done something wrong.
